name: Sasha — excellent hands, two SIV courses, flying for the group's benefit
summary: As strong a skills profile as this questionnaire can record: well past 100 thermic hours, flying weekly in big air, advanced ground handling, 30km-plus declared flights from new sites regularly, two manoeuvres courses, flies out real asymmetrics. Says the reason for the upgrade is that most of the people he flies with are on something higher, expects the new wing to handle turbulence better than his current one, is working on keeping ahead of his group, rough air doesn't bother him, launches when they launch, flies anyway after a long drive, and has had a few near misses he can't account for.
why_this_persona: The 'strong skills, poor motivation' case the brief asks for, and the proof that the psychological half carries real weight at this step. He is Not yet because the psychological category floor decides it on its own, with no gate involved — and he is simultaneously the control case for the 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' gate, which he matches on motive twice over and must NOT fire, because the readiness half of that gate is genuinely satisfied.

notes: Computed skills 98.9, psychological 16.9, total 60.4 plus a 2-point manoeuvres bonus, 62.4. The psychological Not yet floor is 35, so the floor decides the result regardless of the total — and his total being in the sixties is exactly why the floor has to exist.

NO GATE fires, and this is the most important negative check in the set. 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' matches its first clause twice (comparison motive AND 'it'll handle turbulence better'), and every branch of its second clause is false: skills far above 70, phase-aware hands, a real asymmetric flown out, collapse work current, and rough air doesn't trouble him. knowledge/disagreements.md point 9 is explicit that an ambition- or comparison-flavoured motive must not be penalised on its own — it is the PAIRING with thin readiness that both camps agree is concerning. Persona 05 and persona 06 are where the same gate correctly fires.
'ambition_without_readiness' must also stay silent: he ticks longer_xc and competitions, and his skills score is near the top of the scale.

His 'it doesn't really bother me' answer on rough air scores 0.5 — exactly on the Ready-blocker line, passing by the narrowest possible margin, and marked down from 0.55 one rung below. That is flagged as a judgement in meta.owner_decisions rather than a finding, and this persona is where it is visible: if it were scored at 0.45 he would trip a Ready-blocker as well, which would be double-counting, since the psychological floor already has him.

'nerves_are_not_the_problem' must NOT fire. Its trigger is freezing or tensing up, not an untroubled answer — and firing it here would tell a pilot who says rough air is fine that he has a fear problem, which is both wrong and the wrong tone.

'siv_before_you_upgrade' must NOT fire: two courses, current practice, real collapse flown out. He is the only Not yet persona in the set who sees no collapse-related suggestion at all, which is correct.

'resale_and_cost' fires on his Not yet result, and it is the one suggestion in his set that speaks directly to the cost of being wrong — appropriate for a pilot who is about to spend money for a reason that isn't about flying.

TONE CHECK: the 'not_yet_category_floor:psychological' message is the strictest tone test in the rubric. It has to name the question areas without quoting his answers back at him, and the sentence 'none of that is a judgement on you as a pilot' is load-bearing. He is a genuinely good pilot and the result must not read as saying otherwise.
